subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the next steps we agreed on. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Objective we discussed
- Improve the latency and streaming UX for your realtime chat assistant while supporting 200-300 concurrent users during peak.

Key pain points you shared
- Current p95 latency for single-turn generation is ~1.2s (non-streaming) on your in-house endpoint, with streaming startup latency at ~400-450ms which degrades UX.
- When concurrency spikes above ~150 active streams, you see queuing that pushes p95 to >2s and starts dropping frames on the frontend.
- Cost sensitivity: need to keep incremental token cost predictable for forecasted growth.

Current stack
- Frontend: React web client with streaming via SSE.
- Inference: On-prem inference cluster (NVIDIA A40-ish), custom batching logic, and a simple proxy that routes to model VM pools.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes with node autoscaling but cold-starts and pod scheduling add variability.

Success criteria (what Finly considers a win)
- p95 end-to-end token streaming latency <= 350ms for common query shapes (<=512 tokens).
- System sustains 250 concurrent streaming sessions at target latencies without >5% tail-drop or queuing.
- Predictable unit cost per 1k tokens within 15% of current baseline.

What Redwood proposes as follow-ups
- We'll send a short discovery recap doc with proposed test plan and MAP (mutual action plan) for a 4-week technical POC. See attached.
- Proposed benchmarking: synthetic replay of your production trace + live A/B on a canary route to validate streaming startup and p95 under concurrency.
- Initial infra recommendation: a mixed variant routing approach (lighter quantized model for cheap short-turn queries, full model fallback) + prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Next steps / ownership
- Marissa: Deliver the discovery recap doc + POC plan by EOD tomorrow (attached).
- Aditya: Coordinate a short runbook for ingestion of your production traces and confirm format (you mentioned a CSV export).
- Sam / Alex: Share a 7-14 day sample of traces (or provide a download link) and confirm any compliance constraints for giving us a subset.

Attachments: 2027-03-08-finly-discovery-recap.pdf (summary + MAP), finly-map.csv (POC schedule template)

Thanks - looking forward to the POC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
Making inference predictable at scale
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finly.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa,

Appreciate the thorough recap - this matches what we talked about. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 1.2s p95 is measured from our API gateway to frontend render for non-streaming flows (includes network). Streaming startup numbers exclude frontend render time; the 400-450ms is server-to-client first-chunk arrival.
- The concurrency numbers we quoted (150 tipping point) are active streaming sessions measured at the proxy layer; total logged connections are higher during peaks.

On data sharing / compliance: we cannot share raw customer PII in traces. We can provide redacted traces (session id, timing, token counts, request/response sizes, but not actual prompts). We can also run a replay job on our side and share the resulting timings. Which format is easiest for you?

We can commit to a 4-week POC. Goals are as you stated. Alex will coordinate the trace export.

Sam

--
Sam Lee
Head of Product, Finly
sam.lee@finly.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Morning all -

Redaction is fine. For the replay we prefer either a CSV with columns {timestamp, request_id, token_count, model_variant, upstream_latency_ms} or an NDJSON of simplified events. If you can only run the replay on-prem and share aggregated timings, that works too - we can work with aggregated histograms for initial sizing.

Two quick asks from the infra team side before we stand up the POC environment:
1) Can you confirm the typical prompt length distribution (median/90/95 token counts)? That helps us choose model variant splits.
2) Are you using client-side streaming buffering (small chunks) or server-side chunk aggregation? It impacts startup latency strategies.

I'll follow up with a short ingestion spec and example script by EOD.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.inference
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Finly - p95 latency & streaming concurrency requirements

Aditya / Marissa -

Quick answers:
- Prompt length distribution (based on samples we can share): median 45 tokens, p90 180 tokens, p95 320 tokens.
- We do client-side streaming via SSE, and the client buffers until it has ~60ms worth of audio/frames before rendering, which explains some of the render delta.

We will redacted-export 7 days of traces in the CSV schema you suggested and upload to the Drive link by EOD Wed. Also including a short note on our compliance constraints. 

Sam

---
Sam Lee
Head of Product, Finly
